clusters.name: Shared rooms/channels with human-first posting (agents as ordinary members)
clusters.description: Named open or private topic rooms where people post to each other in real time and agents are members, not the default responder. Benchmarks (Slack, Teams, buzz) all let a human post without any AI turn; QM deliberately offloads human chat to Slack.

bestInClass.why: Only source that ships a human-first channel with agents as plain members in source code (q4 SRC); Slack/Teams are equal in product but evidenced by DOC/REA, and QM explicitly does not own human chat.

clusters.mechanism: One channels table with channel_type (stream|forum|dm|workflow), visibility (open|private), topic_required, max_members; a message is an event (kind 9) tagged with the channel id. Posting is a plain append; agents receive it only via mention/subscription rules, never by default. Re-implement: Session Core entry append without an invocation, keyed by space_id, authorized by a Control space:post decision; agents subscribe by mention or engagement rule.

verevon.gap: Every room post is a Model Plane invocation (streamChat); there is no route that appends a human message without a model turn (v-space-backend-002/ui-003 absent, test asserts a plain room turn goes to a model). Docs claim a human-only flow exists: doc-vs-code discrepancy.
verevon.strengths: Room post is a durable Session Core thread with origin=space/space_id CHECK, Control-minted thread:create decision, shared thread listing and audience-revision-filtered room transcript read. Keep this authority path; add a no-invoke append under it.

clusters.benefit: Without human-only posts a Space is a multi-user AI prompt box, not Teams/Slack. This is the single change that turns rooms into a place where people talk and agents join in; it also cuts model cost per message and avoids the default agent answering human small talk.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: add AppendHumanEntry (no invocation) to Session Core, authorized by a digest-bound Control space:post decision minted by the Rust gateway; Frontend: composer 'send' vs '@agent'/'Ask' split; agent turns only on mention or engagement rule (see C043). Application Plane projects the timeline/unread.
clusters.risks: Two write paths for one transcript can drift; ZDR orgs must not persist human text beyond the Session Core retention rule; existing tests assume every post is a turn.
clusters.rationale: Blocks the product vision (humans + agents cooperating like Teams/Slack); table stakes in every human-chat reference.

clusters.name: Direct messages and group DMs
clusters.description: 1:1 and small-group private conversations resolved idempotently from the participant set, hideable per viewer and resurfaced on new activity.

bestInClass.why: DMs reuse the channel machinery with a unique participant_hash so the same set always resolves to one DM; hide is per-viewer projection, not leave. Slack (slack-product-surface-001) and Teams (teams-product-surface-001) also have DMs/group chats; GrokBot has DM/GROUP session kinds (grokbot-agent-product-057).

clusters.mechanism: Open-DM event with participant list; server computes participant_hash = hash(sorted member ids) unique per org, returns existing channel if present; cap 9 participants; per-viewer hide row cleared when new activity arrives.

verevon.gap: Space kinds are personal|room|project|case and create accepts only personal and room; no DM kind, route or 1:1 flow. Personal Space cannot hold other members.

clusters.benefit: Teams-style 1:1 and small-group chat is a core expectation; modelling DMs as small Spaces keeps one authority path (Space access never widens owner-plane ACL) and lets a person DM an agent or a colleague.
clusters.approach: Control Plane: add kind=dm with participant_hash uniqueness and fixed roster (no role escalation); reuse room transcript/presence/read paths; Frontend sidebar DM section with per-viewer hide in Application Plane.
clusters.risks: DM with an agent must bind to the caller's personal scope (see C046) or it leaks agent context; group-DM add-member needs a history-sharing rule (C041).
clusters.rationale: Present in all human-chat references; absence is immediately noticed by Teams/Slack users.

clusters.name: Threads: reply-in-thread, shared multi-author threads, thread panel and broadcast
clusters.description: Any message can start a thread; any member can reply; replies show in a side or focus panel with counts and can optionally also be posted to the main timeline; speaker labels per entry.

bestInClass.why: Server-computed thread_metadata (root, parent, depth, reply_count, descendant_count, last_reply_at, broadcast) written atomically at ingest; clients never count replies; split vs focus panel preference. QM-product-009 is best for the multi-author semantics (any scope member continues, speaker label per entry).

clusters.mechanism: Reply event carries root/parent ids; ingest rejects unknown parents, sets depth=parent+1 (cap 100), upserts thread_metadata counters in the same transaction; broadcast flag copies the reply into the channel timeline; read API returns thread summaries as overlays. Panel mode persisted per user.

verevon.gap: Gateway mints a thread:append decision but Session Core append_message still calls authorize_thread_owner(Mutate), so non-owner replies are refused while the UI offers Reply. No thread side panel, reply count, collapse or also-send-to-channel.
verevon.strengths: Per-turn author attribution (author_subject_id from verified caller only) already provides speaker labels.

clusters.benefit: Multi-author threads are what let a human and several agents work one problem in context; today only the author can continue a post, which defeats cooperation.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: Session Core accepts Space-authorized append from any member holding the thread:append decision (keep owner check for non-space threads); add thread_metadata counters. Frontend: thread side/focus panel, reply count, broadcast toggle.
clusters.risks: Audience revision semantics must hold when a non-owner appends (reader may not see earlier rows); agent turns in a shared thread must use the invoker's grants, not the thread owner's.
clusters.rationale: Table stakes in all five sources; current refusal is a visible bug (UI offers Reply that fails).

clusters.name: Room lenses: forum/posts layout vs chat threads
clusters.description: Per-room choice of a fast chat layout or a slower post-with-comments (forum or Teams 'Posts') layout, switchable with a system notice.

bestInClass.why: Owners pick Threads or Posts per channel and can switch later with a system message (REA, q4); buzz forum is a separate channel type with votes (q3).

clusters.mechanism: Room attribute layout=threads|posts; renderer switches; changing it emits a system message; optional reply-restriction (owner/moderator) for announcement rooms.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Verevon renders every post as a thread card (INF from v-space-ui-001), i.e. effectively a Posts layout; check SpaceRoomTimeline for any layout flag. project/case kinds are refused at create.

clusters.benefit: Project/case Spaces suit a posts lens; announcement rooms need restricted replies.
clusters.approach: Frontend Plane: room layout flag stored on the Space (Control/Application metadata), renderer switch; later.
clusters.risks: Low.
clusters.rationale: Useful once basic chat works; not blocking.

clusters.name: Quoted replies with tombstone and verification state
clusters.description: Reply quoting a specific earlier message (author, time, jump), showing a tombstone if the original was deleted.

bestInClass.why: Quote shows author/time, tombstone after deletion and an unverifiable marker (REA q4). GrokBot has 'In reply to' quote with jump (grokbot-agent-product-058).

clusters.mechanism: Message carries quoted_message_id plus a server-resolved snapshot (author, ts, preview); on render, re-resolve and show tombstone if deleted or 'cannot verify' if the reader lacks access.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; Reply in Verevon targets a thread, not a quoted message. Check SpaceRoomComposer reply target.

clusters.benefit: Gives humans an unambiguous target when approving or correcting a specific agent message in a flat thread.
clusters.approach: Model Plane entry field quoted_entry_seq; Frontend quote chip; reader-side access check so a quote never reveals rows outside the reader's audience revision.
clusters.risks: Quote snapshot could leak content past audience filtering if stored denormalized.
clusters.rationale: Helpful but threads cover most needs.

clusters.name: Mentions bound to exact identities, with group and broadcast handles
clusters.description: @mentions resolve to exact person/agent ids (not text), with ambiguity blocking the send, plus @channel/@here/@team and user-group/tag handles gated by role; one typeahead for people, agents, groups and skills.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: label-to-key map in the composer, recipients sent as structured tags separate from body text, namesakes get qualified labels, pasted mentions verified with generation fences, send awaits bindings. Slack/Teams best for group handles and permission-gated @channel/@team.

clusters.mechanism: Composer keeps Map<label, subjectId>; send payload = text + mentions[] (subject ids); server validates each id against the room roster, rejects unresolved/ambiguous; stores mention records; broadcast handles checked against role policy; notifications fan out from mention records only.

verevon.gap: @agent is shipped (browser sends only mentioned_agent_ref; gateway re-resolves roster and binding). @person is text insertion only: no mention record, no notification (notification-core allowlist blocks it), no highlight; no @room/@here or group handles.
verevon.strengths: Agent mention already follows the exact-identity principle server-side; extend the same mentioned_*_ref pattern to people.

clusters.benefit: Mention records are the prerequisite for notifications, inbox slices, quotas and audit; without them humans cannot summon each other in a Space.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: mentions[] on the entry (subject ids), validated by gateway against Control roster; Application Plane notification-core accepts mention events; Frontend: unified typeahead with chips. Add @room gated by role later.
clusters.risks: Mention of a member who lacks thread_read_entitled must not leak content in the notification payload; ZDR orgs need content-free notifications.
clusters.rationale: Table stakes; @person is visibly broken today (inserts text that does nothing).

clusters.name: Invite an owned agent from the composer when mentioning it
clusters.description: Mentioning an agent you own that is not in the room offers Invite-then-send or reference-only; authorization is rechecked at publish and failures keep the draft.

bestInClass.why: Only source; ownership is not membership, discovery evidence never doubles as authority, re-check at publish (DOC, q4).

clusters.mechanism: Typeahead lists owned-but-absent agents; choosing Invite runs add-member, then sends; any failure aborts send and restores draft; publish re-validates membership.

verevon.gap: Server re-resolution at publish is shipped (roster intersect binding). No inline invite-from-mention flow was found in the baseline; binding an agent is done in the Space agent dialog (INF).
verevon.strengths: Publish-time roster/binding re-resolution matches buzz's rule.

clusters.benefit: Smooth 'pull my agent in' moment while keeping Control as the authority.
clusters.approach: Frontend: typeahead section 'Your agents (not in room)' that calls existing bind route then sends; gateway unchanged.
clusters.risks: Must not auto-bind with broader grants than the room policy.
clusters.rationale: Good UX polish on an existing secure path. Provenance DOC only.

clusters.name: Emoji reactions
clusters.description: Per-user toggled emoji reactions on any message with a quick-reaction row and picker.

bestInClass.why: SRC q4: reactions table with removed_at and source event id, reaction channel derived from the target; Slack (q5 DOC) is the product reference with reactions as first-class events in the same real-time path.

clusters.mechanism: reactions(target_entry_id, subject_id, emoji, created_at, removed_at) unique on (target, subject, emoji); toggle is idempotent; aggregated counts returned with the timeline; real-time event on change.

verevon.gap: No reaction or emoji anywhere in session-core, gateway spaces.rs, Convex schema or Space UI.

clusters.benefit: Cheapest social signal and a free human-to-agent feedback/approval channel (thumbs on an agent turn).
clusters.approach: Application Plane (Convex) reactions table keyed by Session Core entry id with room ACL check via gateway; agent-visible reaction events forwarded to Model Plane only when targeted at an agent message (C009).
dependencies: stable entry ids exposed to UI
clusters.risks: Reactions on content the reactor cannot read; reaction state is content metadata under ZDR (emoji only, no text, so low).
clusters.rationale: Present in all five sources; small effort; enables C009.

clusters.name: Reactions as agent input and output
clusters.description: Human reactions on agent messages reach the agent as typed events (can wake it); agents add acknowledgement or real reactions; thumbs up/down feedback votes.

bestInClass.why: Reactions flow both ways with gating (shouldSurfaceReaction), max 5 per turn, cheap helper model picks an ack emoji with latency logged. GrokBot adds explicit feedback votes (UP/DOWN/SUBMIT/REVERT). QM's text directive parsing (qm-architecture-126) is the weaker mechanism; prefer a typed tool.

clusters.mechanism: Reaction event on an agent-authored entry -> policy gate -> ambient turn input {reaction, target_seq, by}; agent emits reactions through a typed tool (capped per turn); optional cheap-model ack emoji on addressed messages.

verevon.gap: No reactions at all; no feedback vote on Space turns found in baseline.

clusters.benefit: Lightweight human-in-the-loop (approve/retry with a thumbs) without composing a message; agents can say 'seen' cheaply in busy rooms.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: reaction-as-input event type and a react tool; Application Plane emits the event; gate by Space policy to avoid waking agents on every emoji.
clusters.risks: Accidental wakeups and cost; reaction-as-approval must not replace Control approval for effects.
clusters.rationale: Real differentiator for human+agent rooms, after basic reactions.

clusters.name: Custom emoji, GIFs and emoji shortcode completion
clusters.description: Org/member custom emoji, GIF search via server proxy, and :shortcode: completion with locale-aware emoji data.

bestInClass.why: IME-safe ProseMirror shortcode plugin with locale-chunked emojibase data (SRC q4); buzz shows member-owned emoji union and a rate-limited GIF proxy with server-side key. Slack/Teams have custom emoji and GIFs (slack-product-surface-005, teams-product-surface-008).

clusters.mechanism: Composer plugin matches trailing ':' token (1-50 chars) in a 60-char look-back, suggests from a lazy-loaded locale emoji map; GIF search via backend proxy with per-minute rate limit.

verevon.gap: No emoji support in Space.

clusters.benefit: Polish; shortcodes matter once reactions exist.
clusters.approach: Frontend Plane only for shortcodes; skip GIF third-party proxy initially (ZDR/data egress).
clusters.risks: Third-party GIF providers are data egress, conflicts with ZDR orgs.
clusters.rationale: Expected polish, low business value.

clusters.name: Edit and delete messages (with audit and tombstones)
clusters.description: Authors edit or delete their messages under admin policy; owners of an agent can edit/delete its messages; deletes leave tombstones and edits may be retained for compliance.

bestInClass.why: SRC q4 with the unique owner-of-agent authority (human can retract an agent's post) and soft-deleted events kept in the audit log; Teams/Slack add admin policy flags (AllowUserEditMessage/DeleteMessage) and retention-controlled edit logs.

clusters.mechanism: Edit = new revision event referencing the target; delete = tombstone event; permission = self-author OR viewer owns the authoring agent OR admin; originals kept in an append-only audit store subject to retention/ZDR; clients render latest revision plus 'edited'.

verevon.gap: No EditMessage/UpdateMessage in Model Plane proto, no message delete route; only owner whole-thread delete via Chat.

clusters.benefit: Users expect to fix typos and retract mistakes; owner-of-agent retract is a high-trust control over agent output in shared rooms.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: Session Core revision entries (edited/deleted) never in-place overwrite; Control policy flags for edit/delete per org; Control audit receives the event; ZDR orgs keep no original beyond retention.
clusters.risks: Agent context divergence if revisions are not propagated (C012); compliance retention vs ZDR conflict must be explicit.
clusters.rationale: Table stakes; missing edit is noticed on first typo.

clusters.name: Human edits/deletes propagated to agent context as revision entries
clusters.description: When a person edits or deletes a message the agent already saw, a revision entry is appended so the agent reasons over the corrected text.

bestInClass.why: Only source; message_revision system entries appended outside a turn under a lease, rendered to the model as <message-edited>/<message-deleted>.

clusters.mechanism: On edit/delete of an entry with seq < last model-visible seq, append system entry {kind: message_revision, action, target_seq, text?} outside any turn using the session lease; the prompt builder renders it.

verevon.gap: No edit/delete exists, so no propagation.

clusters.benefit: Prevents agents acting on retracted text; keeps model context and audit aligned.
clusters.approach: Model Plane Session Core: implement together with C011 as the same revision entry.
clusters.risks: Deleted text must not be re-shown to the model under ZDR (send 'deleted' marker only).
clusters.rationale: Cheap if done with C011; important for agent correctness.

clusters.name: Rich-text composer (formatting, code, lists, spell-check, Enter behaviour)
clusters.description: WYSIWYG-plus-markdown composer with toolbar, code blocks, lists, link handling, configurable Enter, auto text direction and multi-language spell-check.

bestInClass.why: Tiptap 3 chat-tuned editor with per-surface schema, RTL auto-direction, ARIA placeholder, caret scroll and paste linkify guard (SRC q4); buzz has the fuller markdown round-trip toolbar; Slack the mature shortcut set and 45-locale spell-check.

clusters.mechanism: ProseMirror/Tiptap editor with a restricted schema (paragraph, lists, code, link, mention chip), markdown serialisation on send, Shift+Enter newline with a user setting, dir=auto per paragraph, spellcheck languages per user.

verevon.gap: Composer is a plain textarea; human turns render as plain text; no toolbar or spell-check language choice.
verevon.strengths: Assistant output already gets full ChatMarkdown (code, media, charts).

clusters.benefit: Human-grade composition and rendering of human posts; Norwegian/English spell-check.
clusters.approach: Frontend Plane: Solid-compatible ProseMirror (or Tiptap core) composer emitting markdown + mentions[]; render human turns through ChatMarkdown too.
clusters.risks: Editor bundle size; Solid integration of ProseMirror.
clusters.rationale: Table stakes; human posts rendered as plain text is noticeable.

clusters.name: Per-message action surfaces: hover toolbar, context menu, rich clipboard
clusters.description: Hover/focus toolbar with reaction and more-menu (copy, download, open), native context menu for links/images, copy as text or image with clipboard restore. Class set to common (INF): only GrokBot and Slack have records, but every chat reference visibly has per-message menus; records for buzz/Teams were not captured in this category.

bestInClass.why: Desktop shell provides multi-format set-and-paste with restore and a full localised context menu (SRC q4); GrokBot's toolbar shows keyboard modality but lacks edit/delete.

clusters.mechanism: role=toolbar per message with roving focus; more-menu actions dispatched by entry id; clipboard writes text/html + text/plain (+ image/png) in one ClipboardItem.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check SpaceRoomTimeline for per-turn actions (pin/retitle exist on the post per v-space-ui-011).

clusters.benefit: Daily-use affordances; home for edit, delete, react, quote, forward, save.
clusters.approach: Frontend Plane: one MessageActions component hosting C008/C011/C005/C028 actions.
clusters.risks: Low.
clusters.rationale: Container for several priority actions; cheap.

clusters.name: Rich rendering: markdown, code, math, Mermaid, diffs
clusters.description: Messages render sanitized markdown with tables, highlighted code, KaTeX, Mermaid, stable streaming, and structured diffs as a collapsible viewer.

bestInClass.why: Lazy hljs/KaTeX, Mermaid also in shared views, DOMPurify sanitisation and flicker-free streaming markdown (SRC q4). buzz adds a first-class diff message kind; GrokBot similar cards (grokbot-agent-product-063).

clusters.mechanism: marked + DOMPurify, lazily loaded highlighters/math/mermaid, streaming parser that only re-renders the tail block; diff payloads rendered with a diff viewer.

verevon.gap: Shipped for assistant turns only; human turns are plain text; no diff message type.
verevon.strengths: ChatMarkdown already covers code, media and charts for agent output; keep it as the single renderer.

clusters.benefit: Already on par for agent output.
clusters.approach: Frontend: render human posts with ChatMarkdown; add diff block later.
clusters.risks: None significant.
clusters.rationale: Verevon equal for agent output; small delta for human text.

clusters.name: Typed message content model with forward-compatible cards
clusters.description: Every message has a content type (text, rich, card, file, call event, system, signal...) driving rendering and typed sidebar previews; unknown or retired types render a neutral 'update/unsupported' card.

bestInClass.why: oneof-typed previews plus explicit unknown/retired cards with once-per-type telemetry (SRC q4); Teams REA shows the broad content-type enum.

clusters.mechanism: Entry {content_type enum, payload oneof}; preview projection typed (text, attachments with counts, widget awaiting answer); client renders a fallback card for unknown types and logs once per type.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; room posts are model turns with markdown (INF from v-space-ui-001/006). Check Session Core message schema for a content_type field and whether approvals/tool-calls render as typed cards in the room.

clusters.benefit: Space will carry approvals, receipts, tool calls, files and system events; typing them avoids parsing text and blank rows across client versions.
clusters.approach: Model Plane proto: content_type + payload oneof on entries; Frontend card registry with unknown fallback.
clusters.risks: Schema migration of existing turns.
clusters.rationale: Foundation for agent cards and system messages.

clusters.name: Attachments and file upload pipeline
clusters.description: Paste/drop/attach images, video, audio and files with previews, size/type policy and typed refusal reasons; large bytes go to object storage, not through the app server; malware scan.

bestInClass.why: Content-addressed media (sha256) with server thumbnails, blurhash and client metadata stripping (SRC q4); Slack's 3-step external upload URL + malware scan is the scale pattern; GrokBot best for typed size policy and refusal reasons.

clusters.mechanism: 1) request upload slot (gateway checks room ACL, size/type policy) -> presigned URL + file_id; 2) client PUTs bytes; 3) complete: scan, hash, thumbnail, attach to entry; reads served by id with room ACL check; refusals typed (empty, too_large, count, type).

verevon.gap: Room composer has no file input; Chat has /api/v1/chat/documents and artifacts but Space does not reuse them.

clusters.benefit: Files are core to work rooms and to giving agents material; reusing Data Plane documents keeps one ACL path.
clusters.approach: Data Plane documents with space_ref (Knowledge tab already reads documents.space_ref); gateway presigned upload; Frontend composer attach; attachments referenced from Session Core entries by id, never bytes.
dependencies: Data Plane document upload with space_ref
clusters.risks: ACL widening (room member reading owner-plane documents); ZDR retention of files; storage cost.
clusters.rationale: Present in all sources; a work room without files is not credible.

clusters.name: Speculative attachment pre-upload and pre-captioning
clusters.description: Upload and caption staged attachments while the user is still typing so the agent turn starts immediately.

bestInClass.why: Only source (SRC q5): pre-upload manager keyed by staged path scoped to agent+session, holds/releases, background image captioning.

clusters.mechanism: On stage: start upload, then request caption/extraction; keep a lease; on send, reference prepared ids; on discard, release and delete.

verevon.gap: No attachments in Space at all.

clusters.benefit: Faster first token for attachment-heavy agent turns.
clusters.approach: Add to C017 pipeline later (Data Plane extraction + Model Plane caption).
clusters.risks: Processing unsent files raises consent/ZDR questions; must delete on discard.
clusters.rationale: Optimisation after the basic pipeline.

clusters.name: Safe local file sharing: recent-files shelf and share confirmation
clusters.description: Desktop offers recent local files with thumbnails; sharing a file to others requires a native confirmation; the web page never sees file paths.

bestInClass.why: Only source (SRC q5): main-process capability-by-id upload with native confirm.

clusters.mechanism: Shell scans OS recent list, exposes opaque ids and thumbnails; upload by id happens in the main process after confirm.

verevon.gap: Verevon v3 is web-first; no desktop shell or attachments in Space.

clusters.benefit: Confirm-before-share pattern is useful for agent-produced artifacts posted to shared rooms.
clusters.approach: Adopt only the share-confirmation idea in the web composer; skip the OS recent-files scan.
clusters.risks: OS file scanning is out of scope for a web product.
clusters.rationale: Desktop-shell specific; Verevon is web/Solid; keep only the confirm idea in C017.

clusters.name: Image markup before sending
clusters.description: Draw on an image (pen, colours, undo) before attaching it.

bestInClass.why: Only source (SRC q3).

clusters.mechanism: Canvas strokes in natural-image coordinates, re-encode before upload.

verevon.gap: No attachments.

clusters.benefit: Screenshot feedback to agents.
clusters.approach: Frontend canvas editor after C017.
clusters.risks: Low.
clusters.rationale: Niche.

clusters.name: Attachments as model input, re-authorized every turn
clusters.description: Documents reach the model natively where the provider supports it, else extracted text with explicit truncation/unreadable notices; each artifact is re-authorized per turn and labelled untrusted.

bestInClass.why: SRC q4: newest-first up to 10 docs/8 MB, per-turn authorization, sha256 dedupe, worker extraction with heap/time caps, provider route table, tape stores references not bytes. GrokBot pre-captioning (grokbot-agent-product-139) is the adjacent pattern.

clusters.mechanism: At turn build: list attachments in scope newest-first, authorize each against current ACL, choose native-file vs extracted-text per provider, emit notices for skipped/truncated, wrap as untrusted data; persist only references.

verevon.gap: Room has no attachment path; Chat documents path not reused in Space.

clusters.benefit: Fits Verevon rules exactly: reference-not-bytes supports ZDR, per-turn recheck ensures Space access never widens the owner-plane ACL.
clusters.approach: Model Plane prompt builder pulls Data Plane document refs via retrieval API with per-turn authorization; no cross-plane DB reads.
clusters.risks: Prompt injection via documents (label untrusted); cost of native file inputs.
clusters.rationale: Needed for agents to use room files safely.

clusters.name: Link previews / unfurling
clusters.description: Pasted links render cards (title, site, description, image); either sender-side snapshots or server unfurl with a bounded per-account cache; apps can enrich unfurls.

bestInClass.why: Sender-side fetch under SSRF checks, size caps and per-host cooldown, sanitized image re-hosted, signed snapshot tags so recipients never contact third parties (SRC q4). Slack best for app-enriched unfurls (Work Objects).

clusters.mechanism: On paste: backend fetch with SSRF guard (private-IP block, redirects capped), 256 KB page / 2 MB image caps, extract OG metadata, re-host image, store snapshot with the message; recipients render the snapshot only.

verevon.gap: No link previews in rooms.

clusters.benefit: Expected in chat; snapshot-at-send fits ZDR and the Model-proposes/Quarry-executes rule if the fetch is done by Quarry.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: Quarry fetch-preview endpoint (SSRF-safe) invoked by the gateway on send; snapshot stored on the entry; integration-corev2 providers can supply rich unfurls for their records.
clusters.risks: SSRF; tracking-pixel leakage; ZDR orgs may disable previews.
clusters.rationale: Common and visible; reuses Quarry.

clusters.name: Deep links and entity link chips
clusters.description: Stable shareable links to rooms, messages, runs and external entities that render as chips; links unfurl safely when pasted into other chat apps.

bestInClass.why: Allowlisted entity hosts rendered as chips, scheme handler, agents told to return a link field (SRC q4); Teams shows crawler-UA allowlist for safe external unfurls.

clusters.mechanism: URL scheme /spaces/{ref}/t/{thread}/e/{seq}; client router opens exact entry; chips for known hosts; external crawler UAs get minimal metadata.

verevon.gap: No baseline record in this category; v-space-ui baseline (search section) notes Activity rows link to ?thread_id=... but SpacePage never reads thread_id, so deep links land on the room only.

clusters.benefit: Agents and notifications need precise links back into a room/message.
clusters.approach: Frontend router reads thread/entry params; ZDR-aware minimal OG metadata endpoint in the gateway.
clusters.risks: External unfurl must not leak titles for private rooms.
clusters.rationale: Cheap fix of an existing broken link path.

clusters.name: Voice notes and audio/video clips with transcripts
clusters.description: Record short audio/video/screen clips into a conversation, play inline with speed control, and get transcripts (word-level jump).

bestInClass.why: Streaming STT, TTS for agent memos, word-level transcript jump and speed control (SRC q4); Slack adds screen+camera clips with captions (DOC).

clusters.mechanism: Recorder -> attachment pipeline (C017) -> transcription job -> transcript stored as derived content linked to the clip; player maps word timestamps to seek.

verevon.gap: No voice clips in Space; a voice feature exists in src/features/voice but is not wired into rooms.

clusters.benefit: Async voice suits mobile and pairs with agents summarising clips.
clusters.approach: Reuse src/features/voice + C017; transcription in Model Plane inference; transcript inherits room ACL/ZDR.
clusters.risks: Transcript retention under ZDR.
clusters.rationale: Common but not core to agent work; do after attachments.

clusters.name: Time-anchored video review comments
clusters.description: Comments stamped with video playback time, shown in a side panel, replyable and reactable.

bestInClass.why: Only source: zero-schema timecode prefix on thread replies (SRC q4).

clusters.mechanism: Thread reply text begins with [mm:ss.mmm]; parser extracts it; player seeks on click.

verevon.gap: No media in Space (no baseline record for this specific capability).

clusters.benefit: Design/video review; same trick works for page or line anchors on documents.
clusters.approach: Later, on top of C003 and C017.
clusters.risks: Low.
clusters.rationale: Outside Verevon's core work-room focus for now.

clusters.name: Persistent drafts
clusters.description: Per-room and per-thread drafts survive restarts and failed sends, restored with exact mention recipients; Drafts view.

bestInClass.why: Revisioned local draft store with authoritative-empty marker so late async completions cannot resurrect cleared drafts; restores mention bindings (SRC q4). Slack (slack-product-surface-010) and Teams (DRAFTS slice, teams-shell-and-native-072) also keep drafts.

clusters.mechanism: Draft keyed by (room, thread); {text, mentions[], attachments refs, revision}; clear writes an empty tombstone with higher revision; restore on failed send.

verevon.gap: Composer text is a component-local signal; lost on navigation or failed send.

clusters.benefit: Prevents losing text when an agent invite/approval fails mid-send.
clusters.approach: Frontend localStorage (per-viewer convenience, try/catch) first; optional sync later.
clusters.risks: Drafts in browser storage under ZDR policy must be clearable on logout.
clusters.rationale: Cheap, noticed when lost.

clusters.name: Scheduled send
clusters.description: Schedule a message for later, edit/cancel from a Scheduled view; suggestions from recipient working hours; agent-relayed verbatim scheduled messages.

bestInClass.why: Reuses cron machinery for verbatim one-shot or recurring relays with attribution (SRC q3); Teams has the full human UX (REA q3). buzz-product-024 is a not-built record (kind reserved, no producer), so buzz is not counted.

clusters.mechanism: Scheduled message row {room, author, text, fire_at, status}; scheduler fires through the normal send path with the author's current authority rechecked at fire time.

verevon.gap: No human scheduled send; only agent cron schedules exist in Settings.

clusters.benefit: Minor for humans; useful for agents delivering summaries at sensible times.
clusters.approach: Reuse Control schedule/cron primitives; recheck authority at fire time.
clusters.risks: Authority drift between schedule and fire time.
clusters.rationale: Low priority in all references.

clusters.name: Pinned messages and room bookmarks
clusters.description: Pin important messages for everyone in a room (pinned section, limit), bookmarks/links shelf in the header; agents can manage a capped pin set.

bestInClass.why: Surface-neutral pins API with hard cap usable by the agent (SRC q3); Slack/Teams have the richer human header shelf. buzz-product-025 is a not-built record (kinds reserved only).

clusters.mechanism: room_pins(room, entry_seq|note, pinned_by, at) capped (409 pin_limit); permission = room editor+; shown in header/info pane.

verevon.gap: Only the post author can pin (owner-bound presentation); timeline re-sorts chronologically so pins are flagged not lifted; no pinned section or bookmarks shelf; agents cannot pin.

clusters.benefit: Shared context anchor for humans and agents.
clusters.approach: Application Plane room pins with Space-role authorization (not thread-owner); agent tool to pin with cap; Frontend pinned section.
clusters.risks: Pin must not reveal entries outside a viewer's audience.
clusters.rationale: Existing partial feature with a visible ordering bug.

clusters.name: Saved items, reminders and attention slices
clusters.description: Per-user saved messages with due dates, /remind, and typed attention views (mentions, drafts, saved, reminders, VIP, requests).

bestInClass.why: Fixed slice taxonomy (HubSliceType) usable in hub and feeds (SRC q4); Slack Later + reminders is the best product UX (DOC). Teams saved messages also in teams-product-surface-010.

clusters.mechanism: saved_items(subject, entry ref, due_at, state); reminder scheduler; slices are server queries over mentions/drafts/saved/reminders.

verevon.gap: No saved items or reminders in Space.

clusters.benefit: Personal 'later' list fits the personal Space.
clusters.approach: Application Plane per-user saved items; reminders via Control schedule.
clusters.risks: Saved refs must re-check access on read.
clusters.rationale: Attention category overlap; after core messaging.

clusters.name: Polls / decision cards
clusters.description: Poll posted as a message.

bestInClass.why: Only evidence; REA low confidence and appears app-based (Forms). buzz lists polls as planned only.

clusters.mechanism: Card entry with options and per-user vote rows.

verevon.gap: No polls.

clusters.benefit: An agent-created approve/reject decision card is the higher-value equivalent.
clusters.approach: Build as a C016 card type with Control approval semantics where effects are involved.
clusters.risks: Must not be confused with Control approvals.
clusters.rationale: Weak evidence (REA low) and low value.

clusters.name: Forward messages (incl. into an agent turn)
clusters.description: Forward one or several messages with validations; forwarded content and files are unfolded into the agent's input.

bestInClass.why: Multi-select forward with explicit caps and a rule that bot messages cannot be forwarded (REA q3); QM unfolds forwarded content for the agent (SRC q3).

clusters.mechanism: Forward creates a new entry with forwarded_from provenance chip and copied content snapshot; validation of size/count; access to source rechecked.

verevon.gap: No forwarding.

clusters.benefit: Moving context between rooms and into agents.
clusters.approach: Model Plane entry with provenance; must not carry source-room retrieval grants; Control decision per destination.
clusters.risks: ACL widening across Spaces.
clusters.rationale: Useful but risky for the authority model; after core.

clusters.name: Cross-post to several channels and move chat history into a channel
clusters.description: Publish one post to many channels with bulk edit/delete; move last N days of a group chat into a channel.

bestInClass.why: Only source (REA q3).

clusters.mechanism: Cross-post: one logical post, N channel placements, replies stay with source. Move: copy then delete originals with system note.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; no cross-post or move found (INF).

clusters.benefit: Promote a personal-Space brainstorm into a room.
clusters.approach: Each destination minted as its own Control decision.
clusters.risks: Authority widening; permanent deletes.
clusters.rationale: Teams-only, complex, conflicts with per-Space authority.

clusters.name: Fork a conversation from a message (visibility-preserving)
clusters.description: Branch a conversation at a chosen message; the fork copies only what the forking viewer (or all current members) can see.

bestInClass.why: Intersects visible seq sets of all members under a roster lock, records forkedFrom/forkBoundarySeq (SRC q4). GrokBot has is_fork on its send envelope (grokbot-agent-runtime-092).

clusters.mechanism: fork(thread, upto_seq): read viewer-folded transcript (or intersection across members), append copies to a fresh thread under a new lease, record origin.

verevon.gap: Listed as S1.7 future work (visibility-preserving fork/share) in the QM adoption plan; no code.

clusters.benefit: Lets a member branch off an agent thread without leaking rows others cannot see; reuses Verevon's audience-revision model.
clusters.approach: Model Plane Session Core fork RPC using existing audience-revision filtering.
clusters.risks: Copying content under ZDR; intersection correctness.
clusters.rationale: Already planned and aligned with Verevon's audience model.

clusters.name: Read-only conversation share snapshots
clusters.description: Share button creates an immutable read-only copy of visible messages for 'anyone in org' or 'anyone with link'.

bestInClass.why: Only source; allowlist projection plus creator recheck at read (DOC q3).

clusters.mechanism: Snapshot = allowlisted projection (user messages, final replies, attachments copied to share storage); read recheck of creator access.

verevon.gap: S1.7 defers sharing until resource intersection is enforced.

clusters.benefit: Handoff of agent results to non-members.
clusters.approach: Later; org-internal only first; ZDR orgs disabled.
clusters.risks: Bearer links conflict with ZDR and Space-never-widens-ACL rule.
clusters.rationale: Anyone-with-link conflicts with Verevon's authority rules; revisit org-internal variant later. DOC-only evidence.

clusters.name: Read state: per-thread unread, mark unread, read receipts
clusters.description: Per-room and per-thread unread with divider and jump-to-first-unread, manual mark-unread, cross-device sync, optimistic throttled mark-read, optional read receipts degrading in large chats.

bestInClass.why: Moved from client-encrypted frontier blobs to a relay-side read-state API with manual-unread overrides (SRC q4); Teams best for optimistic 'client lie' + throttled network mark-read and receipt cut-off above 20 participants; GrokBot entry-anchored unread.

clusters.mechanism: read_frontier(subject, room, thread, last_read_seq) server-side; unread = entries with seq > frontier; manual unread sets frontier back; client marks optimistically and batches (max 3 calls / 8 s).

verevon.gap: Room-level lastReadAt only; no per-thread unread, no jump-to-first-unread anchor, no mark-unread, no receipts.
verevon.strengths: Durable server-side per-member marker already syncs across devices.

clusters.benefit: Expected in busy rooms with agent output.
clusters.approach: Application Plane: extend spaceReadMarkers with thread frontier (seq-based); Frontend divider and jump.
clusters.risks: Receipts reveal behaviour; make opt-in.
clusters.rationale: Partial today; per-thread needed once threads are shared.

clusters.name: Typing indicators (including agents)
clusters.description: Transient 'is typing' signals not stored durably; agents broadcast typing while working.

bestInClass.why: Ephemeral events via pub/sub with 5 s window and agents as typers (SRC q3); Slack keeps transient events out of the DB (DOC).

clusters.mechanism: Ephemeral event -> pub/sub -> clients; ZSET per room with short window; agents emit typing while a run streams.

verevon.gap: Delivered by 6 s polling, not push; agents are not shown as typers (agent progress is via run stream).
verevon.strengths: Throttled 3 s beat, 8 s decay, caller writes only own row, no content in rows: keep.

clusters.benefit: Mostly at parity.
clusters.approach: Later: move transient signals to a push channel; show running agents as 'working'.
clusters.risks: Low.
clusters.rationale: Verevon at parity on basics.

clusters.name: Presence, status and availability
clusters.description: Online/away/DND/BRB/OOO with auto-away from OS idle, custom status text/emoji with expiry, scheduled and automatic statuses, status shown when messaged.

bestInClass.why: Richest availability model (calendar, OOO variants, status message shown on @mention) (REA/SRC q5); buzz shows the simplest TTL-lease implementation; Slack shows OS-idle-driven activity.

clusters.mechanism: Presence lease: heartbeat every 60 s sets key TTL 180 s; desktop OS idle > N s -> away; manual status {text, emoji, expires_at, availability}; DND suppresses notifications.

verevon.gap: Room-scoped online/typing/offline only (30 s TTL, polled); no global status, away, DND, custom status or agent states (working, waiting for approval).
verevon.strengths: Content-free presence rows with own-row-only writes.

clusters.benefit: Agents need to know if a human is available before interrupting; humans need to see agent state.
clusters.approach: Application Plane global presence + status per subject; agent presence derived from Model Plane run state.
clusters.risks: Privacy of activity signals.
clusters.rationale: Common; agent presence is a Verevon-specific win.

clusters.name: System messages in the timeline
clusters.description: Membership, agent add/remove, renames, layout and sharing changes written into the conversation as typed, server-signed system entries.

bestInClass.why: 87+ typed system notifications including agent added/removed and history-sharing detail (REA q5); buzz signs notices with the relay key so clients cannot forge them (SRC q3).

clusters.mechanism: System entry {type, actor, subject, details} emitted by the server from authority events, never client-authored; rendered as compact rows.

verevon.gap: No baseline record in this category. Verevon shows receipts and grants in a separate Activity tab (SpaceActivityPanel); check whether member/agent add/remove appear in the room timeline.

clusters.benefit: Makes agent binding and membership changes visible where people work; audit-friendly.
clusters.approach: Application Plane projects Control membership/binding events into typed system entries (C016) in the room timeline.
clusters.risks: Event-to-timeline consistency.
clusters.rationale: Cheap transparency for agent actions.

clusters.name: On-demand per-viewer translation
clusters.description: Translate a received message (or channel) into the viewer's language, visible only to them, with admin policy.

bestInClass.why: Per-message translate with language detection, admin policy AllowUserTranslation, channel translation and language hint headers (REA/SRC q4); Slack states translations are viewer-only (DOC).

clusters.mechanism: Translate(entry_id, target_lang) -> inference with source/known-language hints; result shown only to viewer, not persisted (or cached under room ACL, never under ZDR).

verevon.gap: No baseline record; likely absent (INF: no translate route listed in the Space route table). Check gateway spaces.rs and chat.rs.

clusters.benefit: Norwegian/English mixed teams; translating agent output per viewer.
clusters.approach: Model Plane inference call via gateway; no persistence under ZDR.
clusters.risks: Retaining translated content; cost.
clusters.rationale: Cheap with Model Plane but not core.

clusters.name: Priority/urgent messages with repeat notification
clusters.description: Mark a message Important or Urgent; Urgent re-notifies every N minutes for M minutes.

bestInClass.why: Only source (REA q4).

clusters.mechanism: priority flag on entry; scheduler re-notifies until read or window ends.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; check notification-core for priority.

clusters.benefit: Agent waiting on human approval can escalate by interval.
clusters.approach: Application Plane notification-core escalation policy for approval-wait entries.
clusters.risks: Notification fatigue.
clusters.rationale: Specific value for agent approvals; belongs to attention category.

clusters.name: History-sharing choice when adding members
clusters.description: When adding someone to a group chat, choose to share no history, last N days or all; system message narrates it.

bestInClass.why: Only source (REA q4).

clusters.mechanism: Member add carries history_from (none|ts|all); read path filters entries before history_from for that member.

verevon.gap: Audience-revision filtering exists in the room transcript read, but no adder-chosen history window was found (INF, low confidence).
verevon.strengths: Session Core drops rows stamped with a newer audience revision than the decision: the right primitive.

clusters.benefit: Explicit knob for what new members and agents may read; agent retrieval derives from history.
clusters.approach: Control membership grant carries history window; Session Core read filter uses it.
clusters.risks: Retrieval indexes must honour it too.
clusters.rationale: Matters once DMs/group chats exist.

clusters.name: Reliable send pipeline with honest delivery states and provenance
clusters.description: Optimistic send with a persistent journal, client nonce, echo confirmation, cancel while pending, idempotent delivery (DUPLICATE), UNKNOWN_DURABILITY state, provenance of why a message was sent, and honest 'not delivered/unknown' for external channels.

bestInClass.why: Only source (SRC q5): send-journal states queued/prepared/dispatching/accepted-awaiting-echo, typed delivery ACCEPTED|DUPLICATE|REFUSED and status UNKNOWN_DURABILITY.

clusters.mechanism: Client message_id nonce; journal persisted locally; server dedupes by message_id; bubble confirmed on transcript echo; GetSendStatus for uncertain cases; envelope carries initiator/send_source.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; Verevon append decisions are content-bound (digest), which makes retries hard (per grokbot record relevance note). Check whether streamChat carries an idempotency key.
verevon.strengths: Stop distinguishes recorded vs local-only cancellation honestly (v-space-ui-017).

clusters.benefit: Honest, retry-safe sends matter more when posts trigger costly agent runs.
clusters.approach: Gateway idempotency key per post bound into the Control decision digest; Session Core dedupe; Frontend pending/failed states.
clusters.risks: Digest-bound decisions must include the nonce to stay replay-safe.
clusters.rationale: Prevents duplicate agent runs on flaky networks.

clusters.name: Agent engagement rule in human threads (follow-up without re-mention)
clusters.description: Once an agent has spoken or been mentioned in a thread, later human replies there reach it without another @mention; elsewhere top-level messages are only mirrored and judged in batches.

bestInClass.why: Only source (SRC q4): botHasStakeInThread with LRU and 5 min negative TTL, ambient turn origin.

clusters.mechanism: On human post in a thread: if agent has stake (spoke or mentioned) -> dispatch ambient turn; else no turn. Top-level messages are stored and optionally batch-judged.

verevon.gap: Every post invokes the default model; there is no engagement rule because there is no human-only post.

clusters.benefit: Explainable default for when agents listen in a human room; controls cost; required companion to C001.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: per-thread agent stake record; gateway dispatches an ambient turn only when stake exists or agent is mentioned; Space policy can opt into ambient batch judging.
clusters.risks: Agents silently ignoring messages users expected them to see; surface 'agent is following this thread' state.
clusters.rationale: Without it, human-first posting either disables agents or reverts to every-post-is-a-turn.

clusters.name: Stop a running agent turn
clusters.description: Stop button (or bare 'stop' text) aborts the in-flight run.

bestInClass.why: Only reference record for turn stop (Verevon itself ships it); QM adds the natural-language 'stop' intercept before it becomes a new turn (SRC q3).

clusters.mechanism: Typed run signal abort keyed by thread; text 'stop' matched by /^stop[.!]?$/ intercepted before dispatch.

verevon.gap: No bare-'stop' text intercept (minor).
verevon.strengths: Stop aborts SSE then records cancelled in Session Core, distinguishing recorded vs local-only stops: keep.

clusters.benefit: At parity.
clusters.approach: Optional: intercept bare 'stop' in Space composer.
clusters.risks: None.
clusters.rationale: Verevon equal or ahead (honest recorded/local distinction).

clusters.name: Queue for later and steer a running turn
clusters.description: While a turn runs, queue editable follow-up chips (with attachments) or promote one to steer the running task; multi-author attribution.

bestInClass.why: Only source with editable queue chips and steer promotion with durable RunSignal (SRC q4).

clusters.mechanism: queuedRuns map per thread; steer = durable RunSignal{kind:steer,text,runId}; harness capability check.

verevon.gap: Backend queue/steer shipped (re-mints append decision per queued message) but Space composer disables the textarea while submitting; only /chat uses queueInvocationInput.

clusters.benefit: In a shared room others keep talking while an agent works.
clusters.approach: Frontend: wire queueInvocationInput into SpaceRoomComposer; show queue chips with author.
clusters.risks: Steer by non-owner needs the shared-append authority (C003).
clusters.rationale: Cheap: backend exists.

clusters.name: Conversation kind decides scope and session (one agent, many conversations)
clusters.description: DM, channel and group conversations map to different scopes (personal, channel, group) that own memory/files/sandbox; each thread is its own session inside a shared scope; one agent identity has many sessions keyed by kind.

bestInClass.why: conversationScope() maps dm->personal(actor), group->group:<ref>, else channel:<ref>; threads are sessions sharing the scope's resources (SRC q5). GrokBot's session-kind enum separates agent identity from conversation.

clusters.mechanism: ScopeId 'kind:ref'; Session{scopeId, threadRef}; resources (memory, files, sandbox, crons) attach to scope; context attaches to session.

verevon.gap: Space kinds personal/room exist (project/case refused); a personal Space cannot hold an agent; no DM kind, so 'DM with my agent = my personal scope' is not expressible.
verevon.strengths: Space already owns instructions and knowledge binding shared by its threads.

clusters.benefit: Clear rule for which resources an agent may use in which conversation; prevents personal agent context leaking into rooms.
clusters.approach: Control Plane: scope derived from Space kind; allow agent in personal Space; Model Plane sessions per thread with scope ref.
clusters.risks: Migration of existing personal Spaces.
clusters.rationale: Key architectural rule for agent-in-chat; partly a membership topic.

clusters.name: Bridged external chat surfaces with honest limits
clusters.description: Mirror external platform messages (Slack, SMS) into a neutral store with live fallback, state when context may be incomplete or rate-limited, and tag bridged chats whose features are limited.

bestInClass.why: Surface-neutral cache (channel_messages/state/files) with ingest normalization, mirror-first reads, live fallback and in-band limit notices (SRC q3-q4); Teams tags SMS chats with feature limits (REA).

clusters.mechanism: IngestEvent normalizer -> channel_messages; readMessages tries mirror then live API; context notes when partial; adapter-level capability flags shown in UI.

verevon.gap: Channel Plane is docs-only/future per architecture rules; no baseline record.

clusters.benefit: Future Channel Plane design input.
clusters.approach: Defer to Channel Plane; keep the honest-limits rule.
clusters.risks: Data residency/ZDR of mirrored external content.
clusters.rationale: Channel Plane is future by architecture decision; not part of Space messaging core now.
